teams.strength: Gibbs + Bowers create the biggest combined RB/TE advantage. London, McMillan and Evans fill out a strong receiving lineup.
teams.concern: Jadarian Price is the vulnerable RB2; the bench offers less cover than several rivals. Replace unsigned Justin Tucker.

teams.strength: McCaffrey, Jeanty and McBride give this lineup three premium anchors, with Hurts and Rice adding strength.
teams.concern: The WR2/flex spots depend on Burden and Metcalf; the bench is adequate rather than dominant.

teams.strength: Cook, A.J. Brown, Maye and Loveland make a balanced core. Etienne/Montgomery and useful receiving reserves limit weak spots.
teams.concern: Brian Thomas is the least secure starting receiver; there is less elite RB/TE value than on the top two rosters.

teams.strength: Chase and Collins form an excellent WR pairing; Burrow, Kyren and Swift round out a strong core. Pollard and Pittman provide usable depth.
teams.concern: The Pitts/Tate end of the starting lineup carries less consensus value than the higher-ranked teams’ equivalent spots.

teams.strength: Lamb, Nabers and DeVonta Smith give this roster an outstanding three-WR lineup, supported by Chase Brown.
teams.concern: Tuten at RB2 and Kincaid at TE leave two clear pressure points. Nabers’ recovery adds uncertainty already reflected in the recent boards.

teams.strength: Amon-Ra, Jefferson and Higgins are an elite starting WR trio; Parker Washington is valuable cover.
teams.concern: Jeremiyah Love and MarShawn Lloyd carry the starting-RB burden. RB depth has less established consensus value than the receivers.

teams.strength: Bijan, Pickens, Flowers and Daniels provide a strong core, with Bucky Irving and DJ Moore filling out a competitive lineup.
teams.concern: Jacobs is an uncertain stash, not a dependable starting RB. Kittle’s recovery and thinner usable reserves keep the floor below the top tier.

teams.strength: Taylor, Walker and Hall form the deepest starting RB trio, and this roster has the model’s strongest bench.
teams.concern: Goedert provides little TE advantage; the starting receivers offer less top-end value. Extra bench weight moves this roster up.

teams.strength: Puka and Josh Allen deliver elite WR/QB anchors. Javonte and Judkins form a serviceable RB pair.
teams.concern: The remainder of the lineup lacks another premium anchor; reserve RB support is particularly thin behind the starters.

teams.strength: JSN and Henry anchor a competitive WR-heavy roster; Wilson, Egbuka and Sutton provide useful options.
teams.concern: The Nix/Stafford QB pairing and Stevenson at RB2 offer less weekly advantage. The RB bench is not a major strength.

teams.strength: Achane, Hampton and Olave are a strong trio, with Henderson, Warren and Hubbard providing RB options.
teams.concern: The Mahomes/Goff pairing ranks lower than most league quarterbacks, and WR depth is less convincing. A defense must be added.

teams.strength: Lamar and Barkley are strong anchors, and McConkey/McLaurin are credible starting receivers.
teams.concern: The largest gap is usable flex and bench strength: Lemon, Jones and Worthy trail rivals’ alternatives. Three TEs, two QBs and an early kicker leave fewer RB/WR options.
